reference.title: Trap Bar Deadlift
reference.listing: Animated GIF (title from the catalog listing; the page could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace before the bar leaves the floor, hold the brace through the pull, breathe out at the top or once the plates are back on the floor.
breathing.cadence: About 1.8 s up, a short lockout, about 2 s down, reset on the floor

prescription.load: User-chosen; stop about 2 reps short of failure (RIR 2)
prescription.progression: Add load, then move to the low handles or a barbell deadlift

cues.text: Stand in the middle of the hex bar, feet hip width; hinge and bend the knees to grip the side handles in the middle, palms facing in, arms straight, chest up, back flat.
Brace and push the floor away; hips and shoulders rise together, the bar travels straight up beside the legs.
Stand tall: hips through, glutes tight, shoulders down; no leaning back.
Push the hips back and bend the knees to lower the bar straight down, back flat.
Set the plates down softly, reset the brace and repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back off the floor
mistakes.fix: Lighter load; chest up, brace before the pull.
Push through the whole foot so the hips and shoulders rise together.

mistakes.mistake: Gripping the handles off-centre so the bar tips
mistakes.fix: Hold each handle in its middle so the bar stays level.
Finish tall with the hips under the shoulders.

kinematics.norm: More knee bend than a straight-bar deadlift: the hex bar shifted load toward the knees (higher knee moment) and lifted heavier at similar effort (Swinton 2011)
Hips below the shoulders and above the knees at the start (clinical opinion)
More upright trunk than with an Olympic bar (Stewart 2008, Troy-Hex bar; Swinton 2011)
The handles rise straight up beside the legs, over mid-foot; the frame never touches the shins (clinical opinion)
Controlled lift and lowering; reset on the floor between reps (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #2293, Trap Bar Deadlift, animated GIF (movement reference)
Swinton et al. 2011, a biomechanical analysis of straight and hexagonal barbell deadlifts using submaximal loads (J Strength Cond Res 25(7):2000-2009)
Stewart & Stewart-Menteth 2008, comparative kinematic analysis of the deadlift with an Olympic bar and a Troy-Hex bar (J Sports Sci 26(2))

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
The load is your choice: pick a weight you can move with the form shown for every rep.
Low-back pain: keep the range above pain and the back flat; seek advice if pain persists.
Step in and out of the frame carefully and set the bar down level.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: High handles if you cannot reach the low handles with a flat back.
Knee pain: hinge a little more and bend the knees a little less.
regressions: Lighter plates or an unloaded bar.
progressions: Trap bar deadlift from a deficit.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Hip extensor: drives the hips through as you stand.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Hip extensor: drives the hips through as you stand.
muscleNotes.quads_r: Extend the knees off the floor; trap bar beside the feet (like a hex bar) shift more of the lift to the knees than a straight-bar deadlift (Swinton 2011).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Extend the knees off the floor; trap bar beside the feet (like a hex bar) shift more of the lift to the knees than a straight-bar deadlift (Swinton 2011).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the back flat under load. A hex-bar style deadlift allowed a more upright trunk and lower erector spinae activity than a straight bar (Stewart 2008).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Keep the back flat under load. A hex-bar style deadlift allowed a more upright trunk and lower erector spinae activity than a straight bar (Stewart 2008).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Hold the shoulders against the pull of the trap bar.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Hold the shoulders against the pull of the trap bar.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Keep the arms close to the body.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Keep the arms close to the body.
